newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-J.LEAGUE HEADS INTO CRUCIAL 1997 SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-J.LEAGUE HEADS INTO CRUCIAL 1997 SEASON.

text.p: Japanese professional soccer kicks off a new season on Saturday hoping to arrest a slide in both attendances and revenue.
After storming success in the first few years following the so-called J.League's debut in 1993, support for Japanese soccer appears to have ground to a halt while advancing elsewhere in the world.

According to the J.League's own figures, total revenues in 1996 were 8.27 billion yen -- a 19.6 percent drop from the previous year. The average attendance for matches was 13,400 -- 21 percent less than in 1995.
League spokesman Takehiko Sano said dwindling crowds and a lack of interest from television stations were the inevitable downside of a freak boom which accompanied the J-league's launch.

"The boom is over," he said. "Everyone was interested in the J-league because it was unusual but it's quite natural that, after four years, interest has returned to normal. It's not that interest in sport or soccer has faded away. Ninety percent of fans are young so the future looks better."

League officials also believe Japan's co-hosting of the 2002 World Cup with South Korea will be another spur to growth. They have set their overall target attendance at 5 million -- far less than the goal of 6 million they easily reached in 1995 -- or an average turnout of 15,000 per match.
This year's J-League features 17 clubs with the addition of Vissel Kobe, managed by England's Stuart Baxter who led Sanfrecce Hiroshima to a J-league first-stage title in 1996.
Vissel have a core of experienced players, including Danish international Michael Laudrup, former Swiss midfielder Thomas Bickel, ex-Japan striker Akihiro Nagashima and Tunisian forward Ziad.

Baxter, whose father played for Aston Villa, said he is undaunted by the fact Vissel must play the top five teams in the J-league in it's first five matches, including the club's maiden J-league match against title holders Kashima Antlers.
"Maybe the computer hates us, but I wouldn't change our draw because it will be exciting," he said.
Baxter said his players would carry into each match the responsibility of representing the memory of the thousands of people who died in the 1995 Kobe Earthquake.
"We feel a huge amount of pressure to succeed for the five thousand people who died," he said.
The season kicks off on Saturday with the start of a knockout Cup competition, with the league championship commencing on April 12.

In the two-stage league competition, teams play home and away matches against each other. The winners of each stage meet in a championship final. If a club wins both stages it is automatically crowned league champion.
The Cup championship round starts with quarterfinals on October 15. The final is scheduled for November 29.
